_comment: SoulFire with custom plugins. Based on the official SoulFire egg by mail@pistonmaster.net (AGPL-3.0). Differs only in that the jar is downloaded into the server directory instead of using the one baked into the Docker image, so a rebuilt jar carrying extra plugins can be used.
name: SoulFire (custom plugins)
author: mail@pistonmaster.net
description: Runs a SoulFire dedicated server from a jar built with extra plugins (e.g. Auto TP Accept). The official image supplies Java and start.sh; the jar comes from this repo's build workflow.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# SoulFire (with custom plugins) installation script
#
# Downloads a SoulFire dedicated jar built by this repo's
# "Build SoulFire server with plugins" workflow into the server directory.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server

apt update
apt install -y curl unzip

cd /mnt/server || exit 1

if [ -z "${SF_JAR_URL}" ]; then
  echo "SF_JAR_URL is empty. Set it to the release asset URL of your built jar."
  exit 1
fi

AUTH=()
if [ -n "${SF_GITHUB_TOKEN}" ]; then
  # A private repo needs both the token and the octet-stream Accept header;
  # without the header the API returns JSON metadata instead of the file.
  AUTH=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${SF_GITHUB_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/octet-stream")
fi

echo "Downloading SoulFire jar..."
if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 "${AUTH[@]}" -o soulfire.jar "${SF_JAR_URL}"; then
  echo "Download failed. If the repository is private, set SF_GITHUB_TOKEN."
  exit 1
fi

# The common failure is a private-repo URL fetched without a token: curl saves
# the HTML or JSON error body as soulfire.jar and the server then dies at
# startup with something unrelated. Fail here instead, where the cause is clear.
if ! unzip -tq soulfire.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "The downloaded file is not a valid jar. It starts with:"
  head -c 300 soulfire.jar
  echo
  exit 1
fi

# The dedicated jar carries the server as a nested jar. Catching its absence
# here distinguishes "wrong file entirely" from "jar without the plugin".
if ! unzip -l soulfire.jar | grep -q "META-INF/jars/mod-"; then
  echo "This jar has no nested mod jar, so it is not a SoulFire dedicated jar."
  echo "Make sure you used the uberJar artifact, not the -unshaded one."
  exit 1
fi

echo "Installed soulfire.jar ($(du -h soulfire.jar | cut -f1)) into the server directory."

variables.name: JVM RAM
variables.description: How much RAM should the JVM use? (e.g. 2G)

variables.name: Jar path
variables.description: Which jar to run. Points at the downloaded jar in the server directory rather than the one inside the Docker image.

variables.name: Jar download URL
variables.description: Release asset URL of the jar built by the 'Build SoulFire server with plugins' workflow. Used only during installation/reinstallation.

variables.name: GitHub token
variables.description: Personal access token with read access to the repository. Required while the repository is private. Leave empty for a public repository.
